195: Linux app coordinate clicks support `durationMs`, a non-negative safe integer giving the milliseconds
196: to hold the mouse button down for each click. For example,
197: `await app.click([640, 360], { mouseButton: "right", durationMs: 2000 })` holds the right button for
198: two seconds before releasing it. The same option works for left clicks and keeps the existing
199: bound-window routing. Timed Linux clicks require window-relative coordinates, not an element index.
200: `performSecondaryAction` invokes a named accessibility action; it does not provide a timed

203: Linux app coordinate clicks also support `key`, a key chord held during the mouse click using the
204: same format as `pressKey`. For example, `await app.click([640, 360], { key: "shift" })` performs
205: Shift+left-click. The chord is released between clicks and can be combined with `durationMs`.
206: Linux clicks with `key` require window-relative coordinates. Windows native apps reject `key`
207: and `durationMs` options.

226: ## Workflow
227: 
228: After performing one or more UI actions, call `getAXState()` before deciding what to do next. This keeps you in the current UI state and forces you to re-derive fresh element indices from the latest accessibility text instead of reusing stale ones.
229: For token efficiency, when appropriate, the accessibility tree will be returned as a diff from the most previous accessibility tree, listing only the elements that were removed, added, or changed. Prefer this default diff output; pass `{ disableDiffing: true }` only when you need a fresh full accessibility tree. After a screenshot-only observation, request a full tree before relying on accessibility indexes again.
230: Linux and Windows always return full accessibility state. Linux reports the tree source. `at_spi` elements support the actions listed in the tree; `x11` fallback elements are observation-only, so use a screenshot and window-relative coordinates for input.
231: Minimize model and tool round trips while retaining fresh UI state:
232: 
233: - Batch deterministic actions and the resulting `getAXState()` into one call. You may interact with the UI and return the updated state in that same call, so this does not require a separate tool call.
234: - Calling `cua.getApp(...)`, `cua.getTab(...)`, and `cua.createBrowserTab(...)` returns app or tab bindings and automatically displays the latest AX state after they run.
235: - For `chrome://newtab` (with or without a trailing slash) and Orbit’s signed new-tab extension page, `cua.getTab(...)` displays tab metadata without reading or changing the new-tab page. Use the returned tab's `goto(url)` to navigate to an allowed website.
236: - If a standalone `getAXState()` reports no accessibility-tree change, do not immediately repeat it without an intervening action. Use `getScreenshot()`, `getAXStateAndScreenshot()`, or `{ disableDiffing: true }` only when you can identify missing context that representation should provide.
237: - Prefer a directly relevant result already visible in the current state over opening broader intermediate UI such as “Show All.”
238: - Once the requested result is visibly present, stop exploring and respond.
239:   Perform one or more actions, and then fetch the latest state:
240: 
241: ```typescript
242: await target.click(42);
243: await target.setValue(42, "openai.com");
244: await tab.typeText(42, "hello");
245: await tab.pressKey(42, "Return");
246: await target.scroll(42, "down", 1);
247: await target.scroll([640, 480], "down", 1);
248: await target.selectText(42, "hello");
249: await target.performSecondaryAction(42, "Expand");
250: await target.getAXState();
251: ```

253: ## Output
255: - For text output, use `nodeRepl.write(...)`. The API accepts strings and other values. Use `JSON.stringify(...)` when you want JSON.
256: - For image output, use `nodeRepl.emitImage(...)`. The API accepts data or file URLs, PNG/JPEG/WebP bytes, or `{ bytes, mimeType }`.
257: - The following APIs output their result internally, calling `nodeRepl.write(...)` and/or `nodeRepl.emitImage(...)` will duplicate the output: `getAXState()`, `getScreenshot()`, `getAXStateAndScreenshot()`, `cua.getState()`, `cua.getApp(...)`, `cua.getTab(...)`, `cua.createBrowserTab(...)`, `cua.listApps()`, `cua.listBrowsers()`, and `cua.listTabs()`. Pass `{ emit: false }` to observation and discovery methods to disable their result output. First-use documentation is still displayed. `cua.getBrowser()` automatically displays its first-use documentation; do not write the returned browser object or reread its documentation.
258: - `cua.listWindows()` also displays its result unless `emit: false`. Windows screenshot methods always display images through Sky and reject `emit: false` before capture. With one region, `getScreenshot()` returns image bytes and `getAXStateAndScreenshot()` returns `{ state, screenshot }`. With multiple regions, `getScreenshot()` returns a `ScreenshotRegion[]` and `getAXStateAndScreenshot()` returns `{ state, screenshots }`. Every region is displayed once, followed by its screenshot ID in display order; do not emit the images again. Use a returned ID for coordinate input and refresh it after the next observation.

260: ## Notes
261: 
262: - For browser tabs, `typeText`, `paste`, and `pressKey` take an optional element index as their first argument and focus that element before sending input. Pass `null` to use the currently focused element.
263: - By default, prefer element-index actions over coordinate actions for efficiency when an accessibility element is available. Follow explicit task-specific instructions that require a different documented interaction method, such as using screenshots and coordinate clicks instead of DOM or accessibility-tree interactions. For native apps and tabs that support coordinate input, use screenshots and coordinates when AX actions fail. For DOM-only tabs, use Playwright locators. You can also get a screenshot if you need visual context.
264: - macOS app `paste` uses the system pasteboard then restores the user's previous clipboard contents. Linux and Windows app `paste` support only `text` and use the platform's native text input. Browser `paste` does not restore clipboard contents, and its `md` format inserts Markdown source as plain text. Specify `text`, `md`, or `html` explicitly where supported. Prefer `paste` for formatted content and multiline text.
265: - To type in a Linux app field, use `await app.typeText(text, fieldIndex)` directly. It types at the caret or replaces the selected text. Clicking first can clear the selection or submit the field if its action is `activate`.
266: - On Linux, if you can see the intended field has focus but `typeText` cannot identify it, use `await app.typeCharacters("20")`. It sends printable keys to the bound window without clicking, pasting, or checking which field has focus. Inspect the result before sending more. If a previous attempt entered a prefix, send only the missing text. Use `pressKey` for Return, Tab, and shortcuts.
267: - Native app `scroll` accepts a page count on macOS. On Linux, omit the distance for the native default or pass `{ pixels: 500 }`. On Windows, pass a coordinate target and `{ pixels: 500 }`; element targets and page counts are unsupported. Linux element clicks support one left or right click. Use coordinates for other click options.
268: - `selectText` is unavailable on Linux and Windows. `setValue` is unavailable on Linux. These methods throw before sending input. Use the supported bound actions to edit the UI and verify the result.
269: - If the UI is not behaving as expected, try fetching the latest `getAXState()` to make sure you have the latest context.
270: - `performSecondaryAction()` is for invoking an accessibility action that an element exposes besides a normal click, such as expanding a disclosure row, showing a menu, incrementing a control, or cancelling something. It requires an action actually exposed for that element in the accessibility text. Do not guess action names.
271: - `selectText()` selects matching text in an editable element. Use `prefix` and `suffix` to disambiguate repeated matches, and `selectionType` to choose whether to select the text itself or place the cursor before or after it.
272: - `pressKey()` presses a key or key combination, including modifier and navigation keys. It supports xdotool-style key syntax. Examples: `"a"`, `"Return"`, `"Tab"`, `"super+c"`, `"Up"`, and `"KP_0"` for numpad `0`.
273: - `click` holds each mouse press for `durationMs`; macOS apps and browser tabs hold `key` across the full click sequence.
274: - On macOS, `cua.getApp(...)` accepts an app's display name, full app path, or bundle identifier and launches the app in the background if needed. If display-name resolution fails, retry with the app's bundle identifier from `cua.listApps()`.
275: - `getAXState()`, `getScreenshot()` and `getAXStateAndScreenshot()` automatically wait an appropriate amount of time before capturing new state. In order to complete the task as quickly as possible, don’t pause or delay (ex: `setTimeout(...)`) before getting UI state. Instead, rely on the internal wait.
276: 
277: Persist until the request is fully completed end-to-end. Attempting an action is not completion: verify that the returned UI state visibly shows the requested result. If an action leaves the state unchanged, produces no results, or only reaches an intermediate page, try another approach. Respond only after the requested page, information, or state is visibly present, or explain a concrete blocker you cannot resolve.
